L8: # Ocean Currents Controllercite2† L9: 
L10: HoloOcean worlds can optionally simulate the dynamic effects of real ocean currents on your vehicle. This allows for the testing of more rigorous vehicle navigation or the difficulties that currents could pose to completing a vehicle mission.
L11: 
L12: Note
L13: 
L14: As of now, ocean currents do not work when using Fossen Dynamics for the vehicle controllers.
L15: ## Configuring Scenario for Currentscite3† L16: 
L17: Currents are defined as velocity vectors that are applied to the vehicle.
L18: 
L19: Note
L20: 
L21: This ocean currents vector is in the global frame.
L22: 
L23: Currents are always active, and naturally default to a velocity of [0, 0, 0] for everywhere in the world. There are optional debugging lines that can be turned on within the config by adding the following to the outermost layer:
L24: 
L25:     "current": {
L26:        "vehicle_debugging": True
L27:     }
L28: Turning on debug lines will generate three debugging lines per vehicle, indicating gravity force, buoyancy force, and ocean current velocity, all at the center of mass of the vehicle. The image below demonstrates this:
L29: 
L30: cite4†Image: ../../_images/CurrentDebugLines.png L31: ## Change Currentcite5† L32: 
L33: To change the current during a live game, call set_ocean_currents() from your environment object and pass in the name of the vehicle that you would like to apply the new current vector to, along with that vector.
L34: 
L35:     env.set_ocean_current("auv0", [1.5, 1, 0])
L36: ## Custom Currentscite6† L37: HoloOcean provides a lot of freedom for creating custom ocean current dynamics in your simulation. If you wish to simulate location-dependent currents, it can be accomplished by creating a simple vector field function that takes in location and outputs a vector at that location.
L38: Then, by adding a location sensor to each vehicle you wish to apply the currents to, you can pull vehicle location at each tick, pass that into your vector field function to get current velocity at each location, and apply that to each vehicle individually. Here’s a short example of what that might look like (This assumes that “env” is your environment object variable):
L39: 
L40:     def vector_field(location):
L41:        x, y, z = location
L42:        return [-x, -y, -z]
L43: 
L44:     vehicles = ["auv0", "auv1", "auv2"]
L45: 
L46:     while True:
L47:        tick_info = env.tick()
L48: 
L49:        for vehicle in vehicles:
L50:           location = tick_info[vehicle]["LocationSensor"]
L51:           ocean_current_velocity = vector_field(location)
L52:           env.set_ocean_currents(vehicle, ocean_current_velocity)
L53: If you wish to implement time dependent currents, you can create a new vector field function that takes in time as a parameter and outputs a vector for ocean currents at that time. You can also try adding location to the mix as well to simulate time and location dependency. Then, loop through the different vehicles and apply that current to each. Here’s an example:
L54: 
L55:     def vector_field(time):
L56:        x = np.sin(time)
L57:        y = np.cos(time)
L58:        z = -.5
L59:        return [x, y, z]
L60: 
L61:     time = 0
L62:     vehicles = ["auv0", "auv1", "auv2"]
L63: 
L64:     while True:
L65:        tick_info = env.tick()
L66:        ocean_current_velocity = vector_field(time)
L67:        time += 1
L68: 
L69:        for vehicle in vehicles:
L70:           env.set_ocean_currents(vehicle, ocean_current_velocity)
L71: ## Drawing Vector Fieldscite7† L72: 
L73: cite8†Image: ../../_images/DrawDebugVectorField.png L74: There is an additional environment command called `draw_debug_vector_field` that allows you to render a 3D matrix of vectors to get a better feel for your current field. Just make sure that your function takes in a location vector and outputs a current velocity vector. Required parameters for this command are a vector field function to simulate the current flow and a location vector around which to generate the vector field.
L75: Other optional parameters include the dimensions of the vector field generated, the spacing between the vectors, vector thickness, arrow size scale, and the lifetime of the vector field generated. For more info on all function parameters, see the API documentation: cite9†`draw_debug_vector_field` .
L76: If you want to see an example of this in action, take a look at the cite10†ocean-currents example.
L77:

L6: cite0†HoloOcean L7: # Fossen-Based Dynamicscite2† L8: 
L9: Dynamics for underwater and surface vehicles can be modeled using equations of motion derived in Thor Fossen’s Handbook of Marine Craft Hydrodynamics and Motion Control. Implementations of these dynamics are conveniently provided by Fossen at his cite3†GitHub repository†github.com . We have ported some of Fossen’s implementations into HoloOcean to enable accurate vehicle dynamics simulations.
L10: Using Fossen-based dynamics in HoloOcean is an extension of the Custom Dynamics control scheme. To use the built-in Fossen dynamics, there are just a few steps to configure these improved underwater vehicle dynamics. Here is a summary of the steps to set up Fossen dynamics in HoloOcean with a more detailed explanation and examples in the next sections:
L11:   1. In the scenario configuration, in the agent dictionary, set the ‘fossen_model’ key to the matching Fossen dynamics class. The available Fossen dynamics classes are listed in the Fossen Vehicle Classes section below.
L12: 
L13:   2. In the agent dictionary, set the control_scheme key to the value for custom dynamics for the agent (see cite4†Control Schemes )
L14: 
L15:   3. Setup a Dynamics Sensor in the agent’s sensors list. This sensor is required to read the vehicle state and apply the dynamics model.
L16:   4. Optionally, you can set the dynamics, actuator, and autopilot parameters in the agent configuration. These parameters define the vehicle’s dynamics, control surfaces, and autopilot settings. This is only supported for Fossen dynamic models with a defined configure_from_scenario function defined.
L17:   5. Finally, create a FossenInterface manager object in your simulation script, passing the list of agent names and the scenario configuration. This class is implemented in client/src/fossen_dynamics/fossen_interface.py.
L18: ## Fossen Vehicle Classescite5† L19: 
L20: Currently, we have implemented the dynamics models for two vehicle classes:
L21: 
L22: There is a list of keys that are connected to the Fossen dynamics models. This is defined in the `FossenInterface` class.
L23: 
L24:   * Torpedo (`Torpedo: "torpedo"`)
L25: This class implements the dynamics equations for a torpedo-like vehicle, including the necessary parameters and methods to calculate accelerations based on control inputs to fins and a single propellor. Default Fossen vehicle parameters are currently tuned to approximate the REMUS100 vehicle, as described by Thor Fossen.
L26: 
L27: Control Modes:
L28: 
L29:     * manualControl: Manually set the commanded control surfaces (fins and propellor)
L30:     * depthHeadingAutopilot: Set the depth, heading, and propellor RPM goals which will be handled by the controller
L31: 
L32:   * Otter (`Otter: "otter"`)
L33: 
L34: 
L35: This class implements the dynamic equations for a surface vessel with two propellors at back of the ship. The vehicle does not support to configure the parameters yet from the scenario. Default vehicle parameters match the Otter surface vessel.
L36: 
L37: Control Modes:
L38: 
L39:     * manualControl: Manually set the commanded control surfaces (propellors)
L40:     * headingAutopilot: Not verfied yet by HoloOcean developers. Likely works but with the NED reference frame instead of NWU.
L41: 
L42: Note
L43: 
L44: The Unreal Engine graphics asset is not linked to the fossen model. The number of fins shown on the vehicle will not change in Unreal Engine when changing between child classes.
L45: 
L46: Implementing Fossen dynamics does not change the asset, so the fins will not visibly move when the simulation is running.
L47: 
L48: Note
L49: Mass and other default vehicle parameters set in the HoloOcean engine are ignored when using the “Custom Dynamics” control scheme. The Fossen models account for these separately.
L50: ## Importing Models from PythonVehicleSimulatorcite6† L51: 
L52: If a user has developed a dynamics model class using Thor Fossen’s PythonVehicleSimulator and would like to use it in HoloOcean, they must make the following changes:
L53: 
L54:   * Move the fossen model file into the client/src/holoocean/fossen_dynamics folder
L55: 
L56:   * In the fossen model file:
L57: >     * Change the following import statements:
L58: >
L59: >
L60: > `python_vehicle_simulator.lib` to `holoocean.fossen_dynamics` `python_vehicle_simulator.lib.gnc` to `holoocean.fossen_dynamics.helper_functions`
L61: >
L62: >     * The dynamics method must be changed to return nu_dot (body frame accelerations) instead of nu (body frame velocities).
L63: >
L64: >     * Add a class variable `config_fnc` that is either set to `None` or a function that takes a scenario configuration and modifies the class parameters based on the scenario configuration. See the client/src/holoocean/fossen_dynamics/torpedo.py `configure_torpedo_from_scenario` function for an example of how to implement this function.
L65:   * In the client/src/holoocean/fossen_dynamics/fossen_interface.py file:
L66: 
L67: >     * Add an import statement to import the fossen model class
L68: >
L69: >     * Add the class to the fossen model key pairs
L70: 
L71: Be sure that all other methods and attributes are implemented as expected by the FossenInterface manager.
L72: ## Single Agent Fossen Dynamics Examplecite7† L73: 
L74: In this section we will step through the key elements of our Fossen dynamics implementation and give an example of using Fossen dynamics in HoloOcean. The full code can be found in client/example.py.
L75: ### Configurationcite8† L76: 
L77: Setting up a HoloOcean simulation that uses Fossen dynamics begins with the scenario configuration. The scenario configuration follows the standard HoloOcean format, with a few key differences for Fossen dynamics:
L78: 
L79:   * Dynamics Sensor:
L80: When configuring the main agent, you must include the DynamicsSensor in the list of sensors. The configuration block should include UseRPY: False (default is True; this forces the dynamics to use quaternions instead of Euler angles) and UseCOM: True (default is True).
L81: 
L82:   * Fossen Model:
L83: 
L84: 
L85: The fossen_model key must be set to the name of the Fossen dynamics class you want to use. For example, for the Torpedo dynamics, set fossen_model: “torpedo”.
L86: 
L87:   * Control Scheme:
L88: The control_scheme key must be set to value for Custom Dynamics to enable the Fossen dynamics model.
L89: 
L90:   * Control Mode (optional):
L91: 
L92: 
L93: The control_mode key can be set to the desired control mode for the vehicle. For example, you can set it to depthHeadingAutopilot for a depth and heading autopilot or manualControl for manual control of the fins and propellor.
L94: 
L95:   * Parameters (optional):
L96: The parameters dynamics, actuator, and autopilot can be added to the agent configuration if the configuration function is implemented. Each of these is a dictionary that overwrites the default vehicle parameters. The definitions of each dynamics parameters for supported vehicles is defined in the function.
L97: Below is an example torpedo vehicle scenario configuration that defines all the parameters (matching the default values for the torpedo) for the Torpedo class. A full description of each parameter can be found in the API documentation for the Fossen dynamics classes.

L197: ### Simulation Setupcite9† L198: 
L199: The setup for the simulation is similar to other HoloOcean cite10†Examples .
L200: Simulation setup proceeds first by setting up an environment. We create a list of the names of agents in our scenario that will be controlled by the Fossen dynamics. The list of fossen agent names and scenario configuration are passed to the Fossen Interface. Finally, we initialize a NumPy array of length 6 for linear accelerations (x, y, z) and angular accelerations (about axis x, y, z), all in the global NWU frame.
L201: 
L202:     import holoocean
L203:     from holoocean.fossen_dynamics import *
L204:     import numpy as np
L205: 
L206:     scenario = {...} # See above for scenario configuration
L207: 
L208:     env = holoocean.make(scenario_cfg=scenario)
L209: 
L210:     # Initialize Fossen dynamics model for the agent
L211:     fossen_agents = ['auv0'] # List of names of the agents that will use Fossen dynamics
L212:     fossen_interface = FossenInterface(fossen_agents, scenario)
L213:     accel = np.array(np.zeros(6), float)  # Initialize HoloOcean acceleration input
L214: Note
L215: 
L216: If you are running the simulation live with the Unreal Editor in Standalone mode, be sure to change the additional launch parameters as described in cite11†Getting Started . Add the launch parameter -TicksPerSec to match what is in the Python script for consistent timing.
L217: ### Manual Control Examplecite12† L218: 
L219: To use the manual control method, configure the vehicle mode with the fossen interface to “manualControl” mode. The commanded fin angles can also be set using the Fossen interface.
L220: 
L221: The length of the u_control array is defined in the dynamic model class. It represents the number of command inputs.
L222: 
L223:   * Fin angles should be given in radians. The example below shows how to convert fin angles from degrees to radians using numpy.
L224:   * A positive fin deflection is represented by the right hand rule with a positive rotation about the Z axis. The positive Z axis extends out of the vehicle from the center body frame x axis towards the COP of the fin.
L225: A custom controller can be used with this manual control method to input specific fin commands.
L226: 
L227:     fossen_interface.set_control_mode('auv0', 'manualControl')
L228:     fins_degrees = np.array([10, 10, -10, -10])  # Fin deflections in degrees
L229:     fin_radians = np.radians(fins_degrees)
L230:     thruster_rpm = 800  # not a percent: check the vehicle dynamics for the max RPM
L231:     u_control = np.append(fin_radians, thruster_rpm)
L232: To tick the environment, call the step function and pass it a list of accelerations. Next, send control commands to the surfaces using the set_u_control function on the FossenInterface object. It is not required to set the u_control every tick. If you want to change the control surfaces every tick, set the control command before calling update.
L233: The FossenInterface.update function takes in the state returned from HoloOcean and parses the data from the Dynamics Sensor. Given the state of the vehicle and control surface inputs, it calculates an output of accelerations in the HoloOcean frame (NWU).
L234: 
L235:     for i in range(1500):
L236:         state = env.step(accel)
L237:         fossen_interface.set_u_control('auv0', u_control)  # If desired, you can change the control command here
L238:         accel = fossen_interface.update('auv0', state)  # Calculate accelerations to be applied to HoloOcean agent
L239: ### Depth and Heading Control Examplecite13† L240: 
L241: A common control strategy for underwater vehicles is to control depth and heading separately. This can be done by setting the control mode to depthHeadingAutopilot and setting the goal depth, heading, and thruster RPM.
L242: 
L243: The depth goal is defined in meters. A positive depth corresponds to a negative z location, with depth increasing the further the vehicle descends.
L244: The heading goal is given in the global frame. It ranges from -180 to 180 degrees, with 0 degrees being north (along the positive x-axis) and 90 degrees being West (along the positive y axis).
L245: 
L246: The thruster goal is given directly as RPM, not as a percentage of the maximum RPM. Be sure to check the max RPM in the Fossen vehicle configuration to ensure the command is below the maximum.
L247: 
L248: Warning
L249: When switching to the autopilot control mode more than once there is a possibility of irregular behavior from the autopilot not setting the LP initial position to the current position. This is a known issue and will be fixed in a future release.
L250: 
L251:     depth_goal = 279 # meters
L252:     heading_goal = -10 # degrees
L253:     thruster_goal = 1525 # RPM
L254: 
L255:     fossen_interface.set_control_mode('auv0', 'depthHeadingAutopilot')
L256:     fossen_interface.set_goal('auv0', depth_goal, heading_goal, thruster_goal)
L257:     # Run simulation
L258:     for i in range(1500):
L259:         state = env.step(accel)
L260:         accel = fossen_interface.update('auv0', state)
L261: 
L262:         # Optional arrow visualization (for direction of heading and depth goal)
L263:         pos = state['DynamicsSensor'][6:9]  # [x, y, z]
L264:         x_end = pos[0] + 3 * np.cos(np.deg2rad(heading_goal))
L265:         y_end = pos[1] + 3 * np.sin(np.deg2rad(heading_goal))
L266: 
L267:         color = [0, 255, 0] if abs(depth + pos[2]) <= 2.0 else [255, 0, 0]
L268:         env.draw_arrow(pos.tolist(), end=[x_end, y_end, -depth], color=color, thickness=5, lifetime=0.03)
L269: ## Multi Agent Fossen Dynamics Examplecite14† L270: 
L271: In this section we will step through using fossen dynamics with multiple agents in HoloOcean. The full code can be found in client/example.py. This example is very similar to the above example but with two agents.
L272: ### Configurationcite15† L273: 
L274: See the above example for specific instructions for setting up the configuration for the following items:
L275: 
L276:   * Dynamics Sensor
L277: 
L278:   * Fossen Model
L279: 
L280:   * Control Scheme
L281: 
L282: 
L283: Note that the surface vessel agent using the control scheme 2 for custom dynamics.
L284: 
L285:   * Control Mode (optional)
L286: 
L287:   * Parameters (optional)
L288: Note that the configuration from scenario of the otter class is not implemented yet so no parameters can be set.
L289: 
L290:     scenario = {
L291:     "name": "multi_agent_fossen",
L292:     "world": "OpenWater",
L293:     "package_name": "Ocean",
L294:     "main_agent": "auv0",
L295:     "agents": [
L296:         {
L297:             "agent_name": "auv0",
L298:             "agent_type": "TorpedoAUV",
L299:             "sensors": [
L300:                 {
L301:                     "sensor_type": "DynamicsSensor",
L302:                     "configuration": {
L303:                         "UseCOM": True,
L304:                         "UseRPY": False  # Use quaternion for dynamics
L305:                     }
L306:                 },
L307:             ],
